changes: Fixed the desktop Home view's new-item state initialization

Omi now offers to connect an integration when you open an app it works with — Gmail, Google Calendar, Apple Notes, Notion, Obsidian, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, X, or your local files — with what the integration would do for you and what Omi would read; every connector's sheet now shows the same 'What you get' detail, and you can turn the suggestions off or reset them in Settings → Notifications
Proactive notifications now wait for something that changed, like a new blocker or approaching deadline, instead of repeating a standing status
Added environmental speaker context analysis to detect multi-party calls and meetings from ambient speech
Added voice barge-in interruption to halt playback immediately when the user begins speaking
Made "where was that doc?" answer from the document itself — recent-work questions now resolve to the URL or file you were in, without decoding screen history first

Added Accessibility to Settings → Permissions, so the permission Omi needs to identify the page or file you are in can finally be granted — and granting it now takes effect immediately instead of after a restart
Fixed a crash that could quit Omi while you were using its own window, once Accessibility was granted
Beta builds now use the improved meeting notes pipeline and calendar-aware participant identity by default
Fixed screen search vectors never backfilling for accounts on the new lossless screen history
Live suggestions and other AI features no longer fail silently when a pooled network connection goes stale
Fixed gaps in synced screen activity when OCR or search indexing finishes after capture
Fixed named development bundles keeping shortcuts that differ from Omi Dev
Fixed Permissions showing Accessibility as granted when it was switched off, and added the Bluetooth, Full Disk Access, and Automation permissions the page never displayed
Improved proactive notifications so work updates carry the exact on-screen name or handle when available
Recent-work answers now say how long ago each visit was, in a form that costs a fraction of the previous timestamps
Recent-work questions now answer from the document, page, or file you were actually in, instead of searching raw screen text
Fixed recent-work answers misreporting how long ago you were in an app, and made an in-progress visit say that it is still open
